extracted.intended_audience: readers and prospective contributors to Punch magazine (Victorian literate public; theatre/arts patrons; writers/submitters)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of submission rules and the implicit evaluative criteria and production guidance appearing in a Punch (Victorian magazine) issue — covering contributor instructions plus the magazine's standards for theatre, novels, opera, staging, and rhetorical conduct. Includes both explicit procedural rules and recurring review/production desiderata embedded in reviews and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission return policy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rejected Communications or Contributions, whether MS., Printed Matter, Drawings, or Pictures of any description, will in no case be returned, not even when accompanied by a Stamped and Addressed Envelope, Cover, or Wrapper. To this rule there will be no exception."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firm procedural rule for contributors: do not expect returned manuscripts or materials under any circumstances; send originals only if you are willing to forfeit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment advice: 'Hold' / 'Never cut losses'
rubrics_metrics.description: "I utterly deprecate panic. 'Never cut losses' is the wholesome and cheerful advice I give all my clients... To nine out of ten who ask my advice I invariably say, 'Hold.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance discouraging panic selling — wait for recovery; presented as a broadly applicable, common-sense rule (satirical tone).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical programming: short-service bill recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: "How far preferable, in the summer and autumn season, would be an evening bill of fare consisting of three entrees, each of a different character, and all of first-rate quality. The patron of the drama could pick and choose, and be satisfied with an hour, or two hours, or three hours' entertainment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation for managers: present several short, high-quality pieces of varied character rather than a single long play; expected benefits include audience choice, repeat attendance, varied actor roles, and commercial upside (ability to offer reductions for multiple pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel evaluation: construction, character-realism, literary style
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment phrase: "It is better in construction, its character sketches are more life-like, and its literary style is superior--therefore there is every chance of its not being so successful with the general public."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria for judging fiction: strong plot construction, lifelike character sketches, and superior literary style. Note the reviewer also observes that literary quality does not guarantee popular success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage-management and dramatic economy
rubrics_metrics.description: "As a rule Mr. PINERO'S stage-management is simple and effective: but here the design is confused and the result is an appearance of restless uncertainty... If eight of the characters were cut out, 'they'd none of 'em be missed,' and if the play were compressed into one Act, it would contain the essence of all that was worth retaining..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for a successful stage piece: simple and effective stage-management, clear design (avoid confusion), economical cast (cut non-essential characters), and judicious compression to preserve only what is worth retaining; excessive characters or muddled design are anti-patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opera critique criteria: libretto, dramatic power, orchestration, local colour, casting
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mr. BENNETT'S Libretto of Thorgrim good from literary point of view; poor from dramatic ditto. Composer COWEN not possessing dramatic power sufficient for two, cannot supply the want. Sestett and Chorus... Orchestration shows the hand of a master. Local colour good, but too much local colour spoils the Opera..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluative dimensions for opera: the libretto must function dramatically (not only literarily); the composer must supply dramatic power; orchestration is a measurable strength; local colour should be used judiciously (excess can spoil); casting, singing, and acting are decisive for audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political-publicity tactic: assume impartiality in controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: "The great thing, dear TOBY, in public controversy is to assume an attitude of impartiality. When you have to suggest that a political adversary was privy to the putting-away of his grandmother, do it rather in sorrow than in anger, and if you can find or make an opportunity of saying at the same time a kind word for one of his colleagues, seize it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical guidance on rhetorical conduct in public/political controversy: present accusations with a tone of impartial sorrow rather than anger, and balance attacks by praising others — a tactic to gain moral high ground and persuade audiences.
